title: React State Management Patterns
description: Understand different state management approaches in React applications.

options.text: Redux is required for any React application with shared state
options.explanation: React Context + useReducer can handle shared state for many apps. Redux adds value for complex state logic, time-travel debugging, middleware, and predictable state updates at scale. But it's not always needed.

options.text: Lifting state up is always preferable to using Context or Redux
options.explanation: Lifting state works for closely related components. But lifting too high causes prop drilling and unnecessary re-renders of intermediate components. Context or state management libraries solve this for deeply shared state.

options.text: Server state (API data) and client state (UI state) have different caching and synchronization needs
options.explanation: Server state needs cache invalidation, background refetching, optimistic updates, and error retry — libraries like React Query/TanStack Query handle this. Client state (form inputs, modals, selections) doesn't need server sync and is better served by useState/useReducer.

options.text: useContext re-renders only the components that use the changed value
options.explanation: ALL components consuming a context re-render when ANY value in that context changes, even if they only use an unchanged part. This is why splitting contexts by update frequency and using memoization matters.
